page.title: Event Run of Show for Marketing Teams
page.description: A practical checklist for marketing teams to build, rehearse and deliver a reliable run of show for webinars, summits and hybrid events.
page.h1: Event run of show for marketing teams: what to decide first and how to execute
page.definition: An event run of show is a minute-by-minute production plan that assigns every cue, speaker, graphic and backup path to a named owner so the live broadcast runs without gaps or confusion.
page.quick_answer: Lock the platform and broadcast method first, then assign one owner per workstream and schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before going live.

sections.h2: Which platform and broadcast method should we choose?

blocks.p: Pick the platform before the agenda; the tool dictates what cues are possible and how backups work. Ten platforms compared below, from self-serve streaming studios to enterprise event suites.

sections.h2: What workstreams and owners do we need?

blocks.p: Eight workstreams, each with one owner, cover the full production lifecycle from intake to reporting.

ul: Intake and brief: marketing lead owns the brief document in Google Docs or Notion
Creative and assets: designer builds branded slide template and lower thirds in Figma
Speaker management: speaker manager collects decks, runs tech checks and sends speaker brief
Platform configuration: platform operator sets up Zoom Webinars, ON24, StreamYard or chosen tool
Run of show authoring: producer writes the minute-by-minute cue sheet in Airtable or Asana
Rehearsal and backup: producer runs one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before live
Live production: show caller executes cues, moderator handles Q&A, backup stream runs in parallel
Post-event: editor delivers edited recording and clips; analyst pushes data to HubSpot or GA4

sections.h2: How do we structure the run of show document?

blocks.p: Use a table with columns for timecode, segment, speaker, graphic cue, audio cue, platform action and owner so every row is actionable during the live show.

head: Column
Purpose
rows: Exact minute and second from stream start
Name of block (intro, keynote, panel, break)
Lower third, full-screen slide or video file name
Music bed, sting or mic switch instruction
Spotlight, screen share, poll launch, breakout open

blocks.p: Schedule three checkpoints so issues surface early and the live day stays calm.

ol: Technical check 60 minutes before going live: verify camera, mic, screen share and backup stream
Speaker walk-through 24 hours before: each presenter runs their segment on the real platform
Full dress rehearsal two to five days before: execute the complete run of show with all cues and owners

sections.h2: How do we handle accessibility and backup paths?

blocks.p: Build redundancy into every critical path so a single failure never stops the broadcast.

ul: Captions: enable live captioning in the platform or route audio to a third-party captioner
Sign language: pin an interpreter window or use a dedicated layout in Zoom Events or ON24
Backup stream: run a simultaneous encode to a second CDN or record locally via OBS
Failover host: assign a co-host with full permissions who can take over if the primary host drops
Asset mirror: store all slides, videos and lower thirds in a shared drive accessible to the backup operator

sections.h2: What staffing model fits our event size?

blocks.p: Match crew depth to complexity; one producer can run a simple webinar while summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

faq.q: When should we send the replay to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event; include timestamped chapters and a one-page takeaway PDF.

faq.q: How long does a typical webinar production take from brief to live?
faq.a: Allow two to three weeks from approved brief to live date; a repeat format can move faster because templates and run of show structures already exist.

faq.q: What deliverables should a production partner provide?
faq.a: Run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips.

faq.q: Can we produce on the platform we already use?
faq.a: Yes, production works on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard or any platform your team already licenses; the crew adapts cues to the tool.

faq.q: What is the cost range for a moderated webinar production?
faq.a: Moderated webinars typically cost $2,500 to $7,500 per production based on published ranges from West Peek Productions; summits and hybrid events run $10,000 to $50,000 and above.
